{{Short description|Topological index in graph theory}}

[[File:Harmonic index.svg|thumb|Vertices are labeled by their [[degree (graph theory)|degree]]. The edges in the graph are labeled 2 divided by the sum of the degrees of vertices [[incidence (graph)|incident]] to it. The '''Harmonic index''' is the sum of these edge labels.]]

The '''harmonic index''' is a [[topological index]] based on the degrees of vertices in a [[Graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]]. Introduced by Fajtlowicz in 1987,<ref name="fajtlowicz1987">{{cite journal |last=Fajtlowicz |first=S. |title=On conjectures of Graffiti-II |journal=Congressus Numerantium |volume=60 |date=1987 |pages=187–197}}</ref> it has become an important descriptor in [[chemical graph theory]] and has been extensively studied for its mathematical properties and applications.

== Definition ==

For a simple connected graph <math>G = (V, E)</math> with vertex set <math>V</math> and edge set <math>E</math>, the harmonic index <math>H(G)</math> is defined as:

:<math>\displaystyle H(G) = \sum_{uv \in E(G)} \frac{2}{d(u) + d(v)}</math>

where <math>d(u)</math> and <math>d(v)</math> denote the [[degree (graph theory)|degrees]] of vertices <math>u</math> and <math>v</math> respectively, and the sum is taken over all edges <math>uv</math> in <math>G</math>.<ref name="li2014">{{cite journal |last1=Li |first1=Jianxi |last2=Shiu |first2=Wai Chee |title=The harmonic index of a graph |journal=Rocky Mountain Journal of Mathematics |volume=44 |issue=5 |date=2014 |pages=1607–1620 |doi=10.1216/RMJ-2014-44-5-1607 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Relationship to other indices ==

The harmonic index is closely related to the [[Randić index]] and can be considered as one of its variants. While the Randić index uses <math>(d(u) \cdot d(v))^{-1/2}</math> as the edge weight, the harmonic index uses the harmonic mean of the endpoint degrees.<ref name="li2014"/>

The harmonic index is also related to the [[inverse degree]] of a graph:

:<math>\displaystyle ID(G) = \sum_{u \in V(G)} \frac{1}{d(u)}</math>

== Properties ==

=== Bounds ===

For a connected graph <math>G</math> with <math>n</math> vertices, <math>m</math> edges, maximum degree <math>\Delta</math>, minimum degree <math>\delta</math>, and <math>p</math> pendant edges:

'''Lower bound:'''<ref name="li2014"/>
:<math>\displaystyle H(G) \geq \frac{2p}{\Delta + 1} + \frac{m - p}{\Delta}</math>

Equality holds if and only if <math>G</math> is the star graph <math>K_{1,n-1}</math>, a [[regular graph]], or a <math>(\Delta, 1)</math>-[[semiregular graph]].

'''Upper bounds:''' Various upper bounds have been established for specific graph classes. For example, for trees:<ref name="zhong2012">{{cite journal |last=Zhong |first=L. |title=The harmonic index on graphs |journal=Applied Mathematics Letters |volume=25 |issue=3 |date=2012 |pages=561–566 |doi=10.1016/j.aml.2011.09.059}}</ref>

* For any tree <math>T</math> of order <math>n \geq 3</math>: <math>H(T) \leq H(P_n) = \frac{n-3}{4} + \frac{4}{3}</math>, with equality if and only if <math>T</math> is the [[path graph]] <math>P_n</math>
* For any tree <math>T</math> of order <math>n \geq 3</math>: <math>H(T) \geq H(S_n) = \frac{2(n-1)}{n}</math>, with equality if and only if <math>T</math> is the [[star graph]] <math>S_n</math>

=== Extremal graphs ===

Among all connected graphs with <math>n</math> vertices:<ref name="zhong2012"/>

* The [[complete graph]] <math>K_n</math> maximizes the harmonic index
* The [[path graph]] <math>P_n</math> maximizes the harmonic index among trees
* The [[star graph]] <math>S_n</math> has the minimum harmonic index among trees

For [[unicyclic graph]]s of order <math>n</math>:<ref name="zhong2012unicyclic">{{cite journal |last=Zhong |first=L. |title=The harmonic index on unicyclic graphs |journal=Ars Combinatoria |volume=104 |date=2012 |pages=261–269 |url=https://combinatorialpress.com/article/ars/Volume%20104/volume-104-paper-22.pdf}}</ref>

* The [[cycle graph|cycle]] <math>C_n</math> achieves the maximum value: <math>H(C_n) = n/2</math>
* The graph <math>S(n-2, 1, 1)</math> achieves the minimum value

== Harmonic polynomial ==

The '''harmonic polynomial''' of a graph <math>G</math> is defined as:<ref name="iranmanesh2014">{{cite journal |last1=Iranmanesh |first1=M. A. |last2=Saheli |first2=M. |title=On the harmonic index and harmonic polynomial of Caterpillars with diameter four |journal=Iranian Journal of Mathematical Chemistry |volume=5 |issue=1 |date=2014 |pages=35–43 |doi=10.22052/ijmc.2015.9044 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

:<math>\displaystyle H(G, x) = \sum_{uv \in E(G)} x^{d(u) + d(v) - 1}</math>

This polynomial is named for its relationship to the harmonic index:

:<math>\displaystyle H(G) = 2\int_0^1 H(G, x) \, dx</math>

The harmonic polynomial is also related to the first [[Zagreb polynomial]] 

:<math>M_1(G, x) = \sum_{uv \in E} x^{d(u)+d(v)}</math> 

by the equality:

:<math>M_1(G, x) = x \cdot H(G, x)</math>.<ref name="hernandez2018">{{cite journal |last1=Hernández-Gómez |first1=Juan C. |last2=Méndez-Bermúdez |first2=J. A. |last3=Rodríguez |first3=José M. |last4=Sigarreta |first4=José M. |title=Harmonic index and harmonic polynomial on graph operations |journal=Symmetry |volume=10 |issue=10 |date=2018 |pages=456 |doi=10.3390/sym10100456 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Values for specific graphs ==

For several common graph families, the harmonic index has closed-form expressions:<ref name="li2014"/><ref name="hernandez2018"/>

* '''[[Complete graph]]''' <math>K_n</math>: <math>H(K_n) = \frac{n}{2}</math>
* '''[[Cycle graph]]''' <math>C_n</math>: <math>H(C_n) = \frac{n}{2}</math>
* '''[[Path graph]]''' <math>P_n</math>: <math>H(P_n) = \frac{n-3}{4} + \frac{4}{3}</math> for <math>n \geq 3</math>
* '''[[Star graph]]''' <math>S_n</math>: <math>H(S_n) = \frac{2(n-1)}{n}</math>
* '''[[Complete bipartite graph]]''' <math>K_{n_1, n_2}</math>: <math>H(K_{n_1, n_2}) = \frac{2n_1 n_2}{n_1 + n_2}</math>
* '''[[Hypercube graph]]''' <math>Q_n</math>: <math>H(Q_n) = 2^{n-1}</math>

== Hamiltonian properties ==

Recent work has established connections between the harmonic index and Hamiltonian properties of graphs:<ref name="li2024">{{cite journal |last=Li |first=Rao |title=The harmonic index and some Hamiltonian properties of graphs |journal=Discrete Mathematics Letters |volume=14 |date=2024 |pages=103–107 |doi=10.47443/dml.2024.147 |doi-access=free |url=https://www.dmlett.com/archive/v14/DML24_v14_pp103-107.pdf}}</ref>

'''Theorem''' (Li, 2024): Let <math>G</math> be a <math>k</math>-connected graph with <math>n</math> vertices and <math>e</math> edges, where <math>k \geq 2</math> and <math>n \geq 3</math>. If

:<math>\displaystyle H(G) \geq \frac{(\delta + \Delta)^2}{2M\delta\Delta} \cdot e^2</math>

where <math>M = (k+1)\delta^2 + \frac{e^2}{n-(k+1)}</math>, then <math>G</math> is [[Hamiltonian graph|Hamiltonian]].

A similar result holds for [[traceable graph]]s with <math>k \geq 1</math> and <math>n \geq 9</math>.<ref name="li2024"/>

== Operations on graphs ==

The harmonic index has been studied extensively for various graph operations:<ref name="hernandez2018"/>

=== Cartesian product ===
For graphs <math>G_1</math> and <math>G_2</math>, the harmonic index of their [[Cartesian product of graphs|Cartesian product]] satisfies:

:<math>\displaystyle H(G_1 \times G_2) \geq \frac{1}{2}H(G_1)ID(G_2) + \frac{1}{2}H(G_2)ID(G_1)</math>

=== Other products ===
Similar results have been established for:
* [[Corona product]]
* [[Graph join|Join of graphs]]
* Cartesian sum
* [[Lexicographic product of graphs|Lexicographic product]]

== Graph perturbations ==

The harmonic index exhibits predictable behavior under certain graph operations:<ref name="li2014"/>

* '''Edge separation''': If <math>e = uv</math> is a cut edge with both components having at least two vertices, contracting <math>e</math> and adding a pendant edge decreases the harmonic index.
* '''Edge grafting''': Moving pendant paths to concentrate at a single vertex generally increases the harmonic index.
* '''Vertex deletion''': Removing a pendant vertex strictly decreases the harmonic index: <math>H(G) > H(G - v)</math> for any pendant vertex <math>v</math>.

== Applications ==

The harmonic index has found applications in [[chemical graph theory]], where it serves as a molecular descriptor for predicting physicochemical properties of chemical compounds. In [[QSAR|QSAR/QSPR studies]] (quantitative structure-activity and structure-property relationships), the harmonic index has proven useful for correlating molecular structure with biological activity and physical properties.<ref name="li2014"/> 

The harmonic index has also been applied to [[network theory|network analysis]], where it helps measure connectivity and structural properties of various types of networks. Its mathematical properties, particularly its relationship to vertex degrees and its behavior under graph operations, make it a useful tool for understanding graph structure in both theoretical and applied contexts.<ref name="hernandez2018"/>

== Computational complexity ==

The harmonic index can be computed in <math>O(m)</math> time for a graph with <math>m</math> edges, since it requires only a single pass through all edges. An <math>O(n^2)</math> algorithm for computing the harmonic polynomial has been developed.<ref name="hernandez2018"/>
